chapter_title: I’m Up and Down, and Round and Round
key_takeaways: A circle has reflection symmetry across any diameter and rotational symmetry around its centre.
Exactly one unique circle (circumcircle) can be drawn through any three non-collinear points.
Equal chords are equidistant from the centre and subtend equal angles at the centre.
The perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.
An arc subtends twice as much angle at the centre as it does anywhere on the remaining circle; a semicircle subtends 90 degrees.
In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary (sum = 180 degrees).
